name: APC TransSwap swaps inventory at the live APC/USDT spot quote
summary: The TransSwap proxy's swap(tokenA, tokenB, amount) prices APC against MUSD from the APC/USDT PancakeSwap pair's live reserves (getReserves then router getAmountOut of 1 APC) and pays the output from its own inventory. A flash-loan buy pumped APC, the attacker swapped APC into MUSD at the inflated quote, dumped APC, swapped the MUSD back into more APC at the depressed quote and sold it, draining TransSwap's APC inventory in two transactions.
notes: The TransparentUpgradeableProxy constructor selected implementation 0xc6fc79db585bf2cc613913f3c24b999a676944ac and initialized the MUSD, pair, USDT and APC addresses in the same transaction. No later Upgraded event or configuration transaction preceded the exploit.

Gross depletion of the TransSwap proxy's APC inventory in the two campaign transactions; its MUSD leg nets to zero in each. Each component is valued at what the attacker realised selling it into the APC/USDT pair: the pair's net USDT outflow in that transaction, with USDT at par. The attackers' own dumping moved APC from a pre-attack spot of about 0.789 USDT, so spot-marking the drained APC is not used. DODO flash-loan fees (3,600 and 1,500 USDT) are financing costs and are not deducted; attacker EOAs netted 40,477.142 and 6,126.987 USDT. The second transaction was sent by a different EOA and contract 2,471 seconds later against the same implementation, before the proxy was upgraded.
The implementation is unverified; the pricing path is established from the callTracer trace rather than source.
